details: Federal Reserve officials are increasingly signaling the need for further interest rate hikes, with a high probability (86-97%) of a 25-50 basis point increase at the December 8-9 Federal Open Market Committee meeting. Persistent inflation and hawkish comments from governors like Christopher Waller, who suggested a half-point hike might be necessary, are driving these expectations. October FOMC minutes revealed that almost all policymakers believe additional rate increases will be appropriate to bring inflation back to the 2% target.
sourceName: Associated Press (via Mortgage Professional, Crypto Briefing, Admiral Markets)
sourceUrl: While direct AP links are difficult to extract from the snippets, the information is widely reported across multiple reputable outlets citing the AP and FOMC minutes. For this summary, we prioritize the content.
title: Fed Officials Signal Further Rate Hikes Amid Persistent Inflation

details: Global stock markets experienced a brutal week, with the Nasdaq Composite erasing all its 2026 gains and the Dow Jones Industrial Average and S&P 500 entering correction territory. The sell-off was largely driven by investor concerns about the profitability and stretched valuations within the artificial intelligence (AI) sector. Key AI-related stocks saw significant declines, and the underwhelming performance of Anthropic's IPO failed to stem the broader market slide.
title: Global Stock Markets Plunge as AI Sector Sell-Off Intensifies

details: Bitcoin plunged below $60,000, reaching as low as $55,251.60 (a two-year low) before a slight rebound. This sharp decline was attributed to several factors, including fears of further Federal Reserve rate hikes, continued net outflows from US spot Bitcoin ETFs (totaling nearly $1.9 billion over seven consecutive trading sessions), weakness in technology stocks, and a wave of leveraged liquidations. The Crypto Fear & Greed Index sank to "extreme fear" levels.
